text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me more about the specific location of the shooting pain and how long it has been since your tympanoplasty?

text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. speaker: Doctor
text: I notice you have a history of chronic ear infections and recent surgery; do you currently experience any discharge, itching, or visible rash in the ear canal? Additionally, could you describe the pain more specifically, such as whether it is triggered by touching the tragus or chewing, and if the earring discomfort is due to metal allergy or skin irritation?

text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the pain feel like it is coming from deep inside the jaw joint rather than the ear canal itself, and do you notice any clicking or popping sounds when you open your mouth? I would also like to examine your temporomandibular joint for tenderness.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal TMJ imaging, I suspect the pain is related to the surgical site or eustachian tube dysfunction rather than the jaw. Do you experience any fullness, popping, or clicking sensations in the ear itself when you swallow or yawn?
